AI Use Policy

Version1.0
Effective dateOctober 6, 2026
Applies toWilGlobo Inc. (including TechCare by WilGlobo), all workers (independent contractors, service experts, temporary and seasonal workers, and casual employees), and the public as a statement of how we use AI

Prepared for: %%PREPARED_FOR%%

1. Why we have this policy

AI tools help us work faster. They can also make mistakes, show bias or leak private information. This policy sets clear rules so AI helps our clients and never harms them.

Workers must read and sign this policy before their first dispatch.

2. The law

There is no Canadian law made just for AI that applies to how we use it. The federal Artificial Intelligence and Data Act did not pass. Alberta's Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA) still applies to any personal information we use with AI. We also follow the principles in Canada's voluntary code of conduct for generative AI: human oversight, transparency, safety and fairness.

3. Where we use AI

We use AI for:

  1. Drafting: emails, proposals, how-to guides and reports.
  2. Scheduling: suggesting job times and routes.
  3. Triage: sorting incoming requests by type and urgency.
  4. Content: newsletter, blog and social media drafts.
  5. Internal help: summarizing our own notes and documents.

4. The main rule: AI drafts, a person decides

AI never has the last word.

  • A person reads every AI draft before it goes to a client, worker or the public.
  • A person decides and a person presses send.
  • AI does not send messages to clients on its own. Some automated messages may go out without individual review: booking and job confirmations, calendar invites, reminders, signing-pack emails and receipts. Each one is built from a template a person approved.
  • If you cannot check whether the AI is right, do not use its output.

5. What never goes into AI tools

Never put any of these into a public or consumer AI tool (a free or personal account, or any tool not on the approved list):

  1. Client names, addresses, phone numbers or emails.
  2. Passwords, PINs, security questions or recovery codes. You should never have these anyway.
  3. Photos or screenshots of a client's home, screen, documents or devices.
  4. Bank, card or account details.
  5. Health or family details a client mentions.
  6. Worker personal details.
  7. Anything a client asked us to keep private.

If you need AI help with a client problem, describe it in general terms. For example: "Windows 11 laptop will not connect to a Telus Wi-Fi router." Not: "Mrs. Smith at 12 Oak Street can't get online."

6. Approved tools

Use only the tools on this list for WilGlobo work. Use only the WilGlobo business account, never a personal one.

ToolApproved forPersonal information allowed?
Claude (WilGlobo business account)Drafting and summarisingNo client personal information
Google Workspace and GmailEmail, calendar and recordsYes, for WilGlobo records only
AirtableClient, job, worker and form recordsYes, for WilGlobo records only

Any other AI tool needs Wilton's written approval first. Before approving a tool, Wilton checks its terms on data training, storage location and retention.

Ask Wilton before using any new AI tool for WilGlobo work. Browser add-ons and phone apps count as tools.

7. Telling clients when AI shapes the work

We are open about AI use.

  • If AI materially shapes a deliverable, we tell the client. Examples: a report, website copy, a design, a training guide or a strategy.
  • A simple sentence is enough, such as: "We used AI tools to help draft this. A WilGlobo team member reviewed and edited it."
  • We do not need to disclose minor help like spell check or grammar fixes.
  • If a client asks us not to use AI on their work, we respect that.
  • AI images or voices are never presented as real people or real events.

8. Check for accuracy

AI can sound confident and still be wrong.

  1. Check every fact, number, name, date, price and link.
  2. Test every set of tech instructions before giving it to a client.
  3. Never rely on AI for safety advice. Follow the manufacturer's instructions.
  4. Check that content does not copy someone else's work.
  5. If you find an error after sending, tell Wilton and correct it quickly.

9. Bias and fairness

AI can repeat unfair patterns. Watch for:

  • Language that talks down to older adults, newcomers or people with disabilities.
  • Assumptions about a person based on age, accent, culture or gender.
  • Images that leave groups out or show them unfairly.

Rewrite anything that is unfair or disrespectful.

10. No AI decisions about people

We never use AI to decide anything about a person's:

  • Eligibility for a service or a discount.
  • Credit or ability to pay.
  • Employment, contract or pay.
  • Housing.
  • Health.

A person makes these decisions, using real information, and can explain them.

11. Report problems

Tell Wilton the same day if:

  1. Personal information was put into an AI tool that is not approved.
  2. AI output caused harm, embarrassment or a wrong answer to a client.
  3. You see an AI tool behaving in an unsafe or unexpected way.

Email tech@wilglobo.com or call 403-679-3039. Reporting is not a punishment. Wilton will decide if the Privacy Breach Response Plan (IN-BREACH) applies.

12. Review

We review this policy at least once a year, and sooner if laws or our tools change. Workers will be asked to sign the new version.

13. Agreement

1. Why this form matters

To help you, our worker may need to use your phone, tablet, computer, TV or online accounts. This form explains how WilGlobo Inc., operating as TechCare by WilGlobo ("TechCare" or "we"), keeps your devices and accounts safe while we work.

2. Your passwords stay with you

  • You stay in control of your passwords and PINs.
  • When a password or PIN is needed, you type it in yourself.
  • If you use a password manager, you keep control of it.
  • Our workers will never write down, take a photo of, or keep your passwords or PINs.
  • Our workers will never ask you to say a password or PIN out loud.

If you need help remembering passwords, we can show you safe ways to store them that you control.

3. Your payment details stay with you

  • You enter your own bank card, credit card or banking details.
  • Our workers will look away while you do this.
  • We will never take your card, read out your card number or log in to your bank for you.

4. We only open what the task needs

We only open the apps, files, settings and accounts needed for the job you asked for. We will tell you before we open something new.

5. Seeing personal things on your screen

While we work, we may see your emails, photos, messages or other personal things by accident. If this happens:

  • We will not read more than we need to.
  • We will not copy, save, forward or share anything.
  • We will not take photos or screenshots of any screen that shows your personal information.

6. Remote help

Sometimes we can help you over the internet using a remote-access tool. This lets us see or control your screen from somewhere else.

  • We only use a remote-access tool if you agree each time.
  • You can end the session at any time.
  • When the job is done, we remove the tool from your device, unless you agree in writing to keep it.

7. Watch out for scams

We will never call, text or email you out of the blue asking for passwords, payment or remote access. If someone says they are from TechCare and asks for these, hang up and call us at 403-679-3039.

If our worker sees signs of a scam on your device, they will tell you and help you stay safe.

8. Questions or concerns

Call 403-679-3039 or email tech@wilglobo.com. You can stop a visit at any time if you feel uncomfortable.

Mounting and Installation Waiver

Version1.0
Effective dateOctober 6, 2026
Applies toTechCare clients booking TV mounting or other wall or ceiling installation. Please sign before this work starts.

Prepared for: %%PREPARED_FOR%%

1. About this form

Mounting a TV or other item means drilling into your wall. This form explains the risks and what WilGlobo Inc., operating as TechCare by WilGlobo ("TechCare" or "we"), will and will not do. It adds to your Service Agreement (CL-SERVICE).

2. Your wall

Walls are different. Before we start, we will look at your wall and tell you what we find.

  • Wall type: ☐ Drywall with wood studs ☐ Drywall with metal studs ☐ Concrete or brick ☐ Plaster ☐ Other or not sure: __________
  • We will try to find studs or solid backing to hold the weight.
  • If the wall is not safe for the item, we will not mount it. We will tell you why.

3. Hidden wires and pipes

Wires, pipes and ducts can be hidden inside walls. We use care and a stud finder, but no tool can see everything. There is a small risk of hitting something hidden.

Please tell us if you know where wires, pipes or gas lines run in the wall.

4. Work we do not do

We do not do electrical, gas, plumbing or structural work. These need a licensed trade under Alberta's Safety Codes Act. This includes:

  • Adding or moving power outlets
  • Running power cables inside walls
  • Cutting into load-bearing walls, beams or ceilings

We can suggest you call a licensed electrician or contractor.

5. Permission to drill

By signing, you confirm one of these:

  • ☐ I own this home and can approve the work.
  • ☐ I rent or live in a condo, and I have permission from my landlord or condo board.

If you do not have permission, please get it before we visit.

6. The mount and the item

  • If you supply the mount, you are responsible for its quality and fit.
  • If we supply or help you buy the mount, its warranty comes from the company that made it.
  • We follow the weight limits of the mount and the wall. We will not mount anything heavier than the mount or wall can safely hold.
  • Please tell us the size and weight of your TV or item when you book.

7. Marks and holes

Drilling leaves holes. Moving or removing a mount later will leave holes and marks. Small marks, dust or paint scuffs can happen during the work. We do not patch, fill or paint walls unless we agree on it in writing first.

8. Our responsibility

We take care to do safe, solid work. If something goes wrong, the limits in section 11 of your Service Agreement apply. Those limits do not apply where the law does not allow it, such as injury caused by our negligence, gross negligence, or your rights under the Alberta Consumer Protection Act.

1. Who we are

WilGlobo Inc., operating as TechCare by WilGlobo ("TechCare" or "we"), respects your privacy. We follow Alberta's Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA). When your information moves outside Alberta, we also follow the federal law called PIPEDA.

2. What we collect

We only collect what we need to help you. This may include:

  • Your name, address, phone number and email
  • The name and phone number of your support person, if you have one
  • Details about your devices and the help you need
  • Notes about each visit and the work we did
  • Your booking and payment records (we do not keep your card numbers)
  • Your signed forms

We never collect or keep your passwords or PINs.

3. Why we collect it

  • To book and do the work you ask for
  • To contact you about your visits
  • To send receipts and keep business records
  • To follow up if there is a problem or complaint
  • To keep you and our workers safe
  • To meet the law, including tax record rules

We will not use your information for anything else without asking you first.

4. Who sees your information

  • The worker assigned to your job sees what they need for that job.
  • WilGlobo Inc. office staff and Wilton, the owner, can see your records.
  • We do not sell your information. We do not share it with other businesses for their marketing.

We may share information if the law requires it, or in an emergency to protect someone's safety.

5. Service providers outside Canada

We use these service providers to store records and run our business:

  • Airtable (United States)
  • Google (United States)

This means your information may be stored or handled in the United States. Laws there may allow government agencies in that country to access it. Our payment companies (Stripe or Square) may also process payment details outside Canada.

If you have questions about how these service providers handle your information, contact our privacy contact in section 9.

6. How we protect it

  • Only people who need your information can see it.
  • Accounts are protected with passwords and two-step sign-in.
  • Workers do not keep your information on their own phones or notebooks after a job.

If a privacy breach creates a real risk of significant harm to you, we will report it to the Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Alberta. We will tell you if we are required to.

7. How long we keep it

We keep your information only as long as we reasonably need it. Business and tax records are kept for 6 years, as the Canada Revenue Agency requires. After that, we delete or destroy it safely.

8. Your rights

You can:

  • Ask to see the information we hold about you
  • Ask us to correct anything that is wrong
  • Ask how we have used or shared it

Send your request to our privacy contact. We will answer within 45 days, as PIPA requires. If you are not happy with our answer, you can contact the Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Alberta.

9. Privacy contact

  • Name: Wilton, Privacy Officer, WilGlobo Inc.
  • Email: tech@wilglobo.com

  • Mail: 105 26 Ave SW, Calgary, Alberta

1. Who we are

This agreement is between you (the client) and WilGlobo Inc., operating as TechCare by WilGlobo. In this agreement, "TechCare" or "we" means WilGlobo Inc.

  • Address: 105 26 Ave SW, Calgary, Alberta
  • Email: tech@wilglobo.com

  • Website: techcares.ca

Please read this carefully. You are welcome to have a family member, friend or support person read it with you. Ask us about anything that is not clear before you sign.

2. What we do

We help you with your home technology. This can include:

  • Setting up phones, tablets, computers and apps
  • Setting up email
  • Help with buying or renting a device
  • Following up with your internet, TV, phone or subscription companies
  • Wi-Fi and network setup
  • TV setup and TV mounting
  • Windows installation and troubleshooting

3. What we do not do

  • We do not do electrical, gas, plumbing or structural work. These need a licensed trade.
  • We do not give financial, legal, investment or medical advice.
  • We do not handle your bank card or credit card details. You enter your own payment information.
  • We do not ask for, write down or keep your passwords or PINs.
  • We do not accept gifts, loans or money for ourselves. All payments go to WilGlobo Inc.
  • We do not repair hardware inside a device unless we agree on it in writing first.

4. Pricing

We charge per task. Some work is priced per project, as a package, or by the hour.

  • Basic tasks usually cost $35 to $45.
  • Advanced tasks start at $55.

We will tell you the price and confirm it with you before any work starts. If we find the job is bigger than expected, we stop and talk to you first. We will not go ahead with extra cost unless you agree.

5. Payment

  • You pay WilGlobo Inc. directly. You can pay by debit or credit card (processed by Square or Stripe) or by Interac e-Transfer. Details are on your invoice.
  • Payment is due when the task is completed, unless we agree otherwise in writing before the work starts.
  • Please never pay a worker in cash or give a worker money directly.
  • You will get a receipt from WilGlobo Inc.

6. No new work sold in your home

Our workers will not sell you new paid work or book new paid jobs while they are in your home. If you need more help, we will give you a quote later by phone, email or online. You can then decide in your own time.

7. Your responsibilities

To help us do a good job, you agree to:

  1. Back up your photos, files and other important data before we start, or ask us to help you plan a backup first.
  2. Own or hold a proper licence for any software we install or set up for you.
  3. Be at home during the visit, or have a trusted support person there.
  4. Tell us about any known problems with the device, wall or space before we start.
  5. Keep your passwords and PINs private and type them in yourself.

8. Problems that were already there

Some devices have faults before we arrive. These can include old parts, damage, viruses or failing batteries. We are not responsible for faults that existed before our visit. If we notice one, we will tell you.

9. Other companies' products and services

Devices, apps, software and subscriptions are made or sold by other companies. Their warranties, terms and prices are between you and that company. We do not give a warranty on their products or services. We can help you contact them.

10. Risk of data loss

Working on any device carries some risk. Files, settings or photos can be lost, even when everyone is careful. By signing, you understand this risk. This is why backing up first (section 7) is so important.

11. Limit on what we owe you

If something goes wrong because of our work, the most we will pay is the amount you paid us for that task.

This limit does not apply where the law does not allow it. That means it does not apply to:

  • Injury to a person caused by our negligence
  • Gross negligence
  • Any of your rights under the Alberta Consumer Protection Act that cannot be given up

Nothing in this agreement takes away a right that the law says you cannot give up.

12. Cancelling a visit

Please give us at least 24 hours' notice if you need to cancel or move a visit. There is no fee for cancelling. If late cancellations or missed visits happen more than twice, we may ask for payment before future visits.

You can cancel a booked visit by phone or email. If you cancel a job before work starts, you do not pay for that job.

If we need to cancel, we will call you as soon as we can and rebook at no cost to you.

13. If you are not happy

Please tell us. We want to fix it.

  1. Call 403-679-3039 or email tech@wilglobo.com.
  2. Tell us what happened and what you would like us to do.
  3. We will reply within 2 business days.

Full steps are in our Service Terms, Pricing and Complaints document (PB-TERMS). You can ask for a printed or large-print copy.

14. Electronic signature

You can sign this agreement by typing your name on our web form. Under the Alberta Electronic Transactions Act, this is a valid signature. We record the date, time and version of this document.

15. Law that applies

This agreement follows the laws of Alberta and the laws of Canada that apply in Alberta.

Applies toAll independent contractors, part-time service experts and temporary or seasonal workers who do work for WilGlobo Inc. (including TechCare by WilGlobo). Must be signed before first dispatch.

Prepared for: %%PREPARED_FOR%%

1. The parties

This agreement is between:

  1. WilGlobo Inc., operating as TechCare by WilGlobo, 105 26 Ave SW, Calgary, Alberta. Contact: tech@wilglobo.com, 403-679-3039. In this agreement, "WilGlobo" or "we".
  2. The person or business named in the signature block. In this agreement, "you".

This agreement covers all WilGlobo services you may be offered. That includes TechCare home tech help, digital and AI consulting, and creative and media work.

2. What this agreement does

  1. It sets the terms for jobs we may offer you from time to time.
  2. It does not promise you any amount of work. It does not require you to accept any job.
  3. Every job is an offer. You may accept or decline each offer through the job update link. A job you accept is confirmed by a calendar invite and email. That job confirmation, plus this agreement, forms the contract for that job.
  4. If a job confirmation and this agreement conflict, this agreement wins unless the job confirmation says otherwise in writing.
  5. This agreement is for independent contractors only. If you will work regular scheduled hours for WilGlobo, you are engaged as a casual employee under the Casual Employment Letter (WK-CASUAL) instead, not under this agreement.

3. Your independent status

You are not an employee of WilGlobo. You run your own business. That means:

  1. You supply your own tools, equipment, vehicle and phone, unless a job confirmation says we will supply something.
  2. You decide which jobs to accept. You may decline any job offered, without giving a reason and without penalty.
  3. You set your own availability. Once you accept a job, you agree to attend at the confirmed time or give notice as set out in section 13.
  4. You may work for other businesses and clients, including in the same field, subject to section 8.
  5. You are responsible for your own income tax, CPP contributions and any EI premiums that apply to self-employed people. We will not deduct tax from your pay.
  6. You are responsible for GST. If your taxable supplies pass $30,000 in four consecutive calendar quarters, you must register for GST and charge it. Tell us your GST number when you register.
  7. You must keep a valid WCB-Alberta clearance letter, or your own WCB coverage, for as long as you do work for us. If you do not, WilGlobo may be charged your premiums as principal. We may hold back that amount from your pay.
  8. You must carry commercial general liability insurance of at least $2,000,000 per occurrence. We ask to be named as an additional insured where your insurer allows it. Give us a certificate before first dispatch and each time it renews.
  9. You may hire your own helper only with our written approval for that job. Any helper must meet the same checks and sign the same WK documents.

Why your status matters

The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) decides whether someone is an employee or self-employed by looking at the real working relationship, not just the words in a contract. CRA guide RC4110 looks at:

  1. Control. Who decides how, when and where the work is done?
  2. Tools and equipment. Who supplies and pays for them?
  3. Chance of profit and risk of loss. Can you earn more by working efficiently? Do you carry your own costs?
  4. Integration. Are you running your own business, or are you part of ours?

We have to set some rules. These include safety rules, privacy rules and how we protect seniors in their homes. Some of those rules look like control. They exist because the law and our clients require them, not to direct how you run your business.

Be honest with yourself. If you work only for us, on our schedule, with our tools, CRA may see you as an employee. That has tax and payroll results for both of us. If anything in how we work together starts to feel like employment, tell us. Either of us may ask CRA for a ruling on your status, using form CPT1. Get your own tax advice if you are unsure.

4. Rates

  1. Your rate is set for each job in writing before you start. By default, you are paid a flat fee:
  2. per task (a fixed amount for a defined task), or
  3. per project (a fixed amount for a defined scope).

We pay hourly only when the job confirmation says so. Hourly pay covers time actually worked, as recorded in the job status form.

  1. The rate in the job confirmation is the full amount we will pay for that job, plus GST if you are registered.
  2. Travel time, parking and mileage are not paid unless the job confirmation says so.
  3. Extra work found on site is not paid unless we approve it in writing before you do it. See section 7.
  4. Clients pay WilGlobo. You must not take payment, cash tips or any other money from a client. Do not accept anything beyond a coffee or a small snack offered during the visit. See WK-CONDUCT.

5. How and when we pay you

  1. We pay you every two weeks, on Friday, for jobs marked completed and invoiced by the Sunday before.
  2. We pay by Interac e-Transfer or direct deposit.
  3. A job counts as completed when you have marked it complete in the job status form and the client has not reported a problem within 2 business days.
  4. If a client disputes the work, we may hold payment for that job while we look into it. We will tell you within 5 business days and work it out with you fairly.
  5. Our payment to you does not depend on whether the client has paid us, unless the job confirmation says otherwise.

6. Invoices and records

  1. Send an invoice for each pay cycle. Include your name or business name, GST number if registered, job references, dates, rate and total.
  2. We may supply a self-billing statement instead. If you accept it, you must check it and tell us of any error within 7 days.
  3. Keep your own business records for at least 6 years, as CRA requires.
  4. Update the job status form at arrival and departure and when the job is finished. These records support your pay and the Working Alone check-in in WK-SAFETY.

7. Extra work and selling in the home

  1. You must never sell, quote or book new paid work while in a client's home.
  2. If the client asks for more help, write it in the job status form. WilGlobo will quote and book it afterwards by phone, email or online.
  3. This protects clients and keeps WilGlobo within Alberta consumer protection rules on sales made in the home.

8. Non-solicitation of WilGlobo clients

  1. While this agreement is in force, and for 12 months after it ends, you must not offer or provide private paid services to any client you met through WilGlobo, unless we agree in writing.
  2. This applies whether you approach the client or the client approaches you. If a client asks you directly, refer them to WilGlobo.
  3. This does not stop you from serving people you already served before you met them through us. Tell us about any such person at the start.
  4. This clause is limited to WilGlobo clients. It does not stop you working in your field.

9. Confidentiality and privacy

You must follow WK-PRIVACY (Confidentiality and Privacy Undertaking). It is part of this agreement. Your duties under it continue after this agreement ends.

10. Conduct and safety

You must follow:

  1. WK-CONDUCT (Code of Conduct, Ethics and Client Safeguarding),
  2. WK-SAFETY (Health and Safety Rules), and
  3. AI-POLICY (WilGlobo AI Use Policy), for any work that uses AI tools.

These documents are part of this agreement.

11. Ownership of work (creative, digital and AI work)

  1. Anything you create for a job belongs to WilGlobo, or to the client if the job confirmation says so, once you have been paid for it. This includes designs, writing, video, code, prompts, AI outputs, settings files and documentation.
  2. You assign all copyright and other rights in that work on payment. You waive your moral rights in it to the extent the law allows.
  3. You keep ownership of your own tools, templates and know-how that existed before the job. You give WilGlobo and the client a free, permanent licence to use any of them that are built into the delivered work.
  4. You must not use third-party material, fonts, images or music unless you have the right to, and you must tell us of any licence terms.
  5. You confirm that the work is your own or properly licensed, and that you disclosed any use of AI tools as AI-POLICY requires.

12. Responsibility for loss (indemnity)

  1. Each of us is responsible for loss caused by our own negligence, breach of this agreement or breach of law.
  2. You agree to cover WilGlobo for claims, costs and losses to the extent they are caused by your negligence, wilful misconduct, or breach of this agreement, WK-CONDUCT, WK-PRIVACY or WK-SAFETY.
  3. WilGlobo agrees to cover you for claims to the extent they are caused by our negligence or our breach of this agreement.
  4. If both of us share fault, each pays its fair share.
  5. You must tell us right away about any damage, injury or complaint, using the Incident Report form.

13. Ending the agreement

  1. Either of us may end this agreement by giving 14 days' written notice by email.
  2. We may end it right away, without notice, if you:
  3. breach WK-CONDUCT, WK-PRIVACY or WK-SAFETY in a serious way,
  4. harm, threaten, exploit or take money or property from a client,
  5. fail or lose your police check, insurance or WCB clearance, or
  6. act dishonestly with us or a client.
  7. If you cannot attend an accepted job, tell us as soon as you know, and at least 24 hours before, except in an emergency.
  8. When this agreement ends, we pay you for work completed up to that date. You must return or delete client information as WK-PRIVACY requires, and return any WilGlobo equipment.
  9. Sections 8, 9, 11 and 12 continue after this agreement ends.

14. Police check (vulnerable sector)

  1. Before first dispatch you must give us a current police information check with a vulnerable sector check. It must be dated within 6 months of your start.
  2. You must renew it every 3 years.
  3. You must tell us right away if you are charged with or convicted of any offence after your check.
  4. We decide whether a result is compatible with work in seniors' homes. We may limit you to jobs that are not in homes.

15. Variants

15.1 Part-time service expert

If you are engaged as a part-time service expert on a set contract:

  1. The contract term is set out in your written schedule.
  2. The services and expected volume are set out in a written schedule attached to this agreement.
  3. You may still decline individual jobs, but you agree to give us your available times as set out in your written schedule.
  4. Pay basis is per task or per contract as set out in the schedule.

15.2 Temporary or seasonal worker

If you are engaged for a temporary or seasonal period:

  1. The engagement starts and ends on the dates set out in your written schedule, unless both of us agree in writing to extend it.
  2. The agreement ends automatically on the end date. No notice is needed.
  3. All checks, insurance, WCB clearance and WK documents still apply.
  4. Note for WilGlobo: a short fixed-term role with set hours and our tools is more likely to be employment. Check the CRA questions in IN-ONBOARD before using this variant. If the role has regular scheduled hours, use WK-CASUAL instead.

16. General

  1. This agreement, the job confirmations and the WK documents and AI-POLICY are the whole agreement between us.
  2. Changes must be in writing. We may update WK-CONDUCT, WK-PRIVACY or WK-SAFETY with 14 days' notice. You will be asked to sign the new version before your next job.
  3. Alberta law applies.
  4. You agree that this agreement may be signed electronically, as allowed by the Alberta Electronic Transactions Act. Your typed name is your signature.
  5. If one part of this agreement is not enforceable, the rest still applies.

Code of Conduct, Ethics and Client Safeguarding

Version1.0
Effective dateOctober 6, 2026
Applies toAll contractors, service experts, temporary or seasonal workers and casual employees of WilGlobo Inc. (including TechCare by WilGlobo). Must be signed before first dispatch.

Prepared for: %%PREPARED_FOR%%

1. Why this code exists

Many of our clients are adults 50 and over. We serve them in their homes. They trust us with their devices, their accounts and their space.

This code tells you how to earn and keep that trust. It is part of your Worker Services Agreement (WK-AGREEMENT), or your Casual Employment Letter (WK-CASUAL) if you are a casual employee.

2. In-home visits: DOs

  1. Call the client 30 minutes before you arrive. Confirm the time and your name.
  2. Arrive on time. If you will be late, call the client and update the job status form.
  3. Wear your TechCare ID badge where the client can see it. Say your name and "TechCare by WilGlobo" at the door.
  4. Wait to be invited in.
  5. Ask about footwear. Remove your shoes or use shoe covers if the client prefers.
  6. Ask before you touch anything. Explain what you are about to do in plain words.
  7. Ask if there are pets. Ask the client to secure any pet that makes you or the work unsafe.
  8. Welcome a support person. A family member, friend or neighbour may stay for the whole visit.
  9. Leave doors in the position the client wants. If the client seems uneasy being alone with you, offer to keep a door open or invite a support person.
  10. Be patient. Go at the client's pace. Check that they understand before you move on.
  11. Leave the space as you found it. Take your packaging and debris with you.
  12. Check in on the job status form at arrival and departure, as WK-SAFETY requires.

3. In-home visits: DON'Ts

  1. Do not smoke, vape, use cannabis or drink alcohol before or during a visit, or on the client's property.
  2. Do not arrive impaired by anything, including medication that affects your judgment.
  3. Do not use the client's phone, computer, Wi-Fi for your own use, washroom, kitchen or food without asking first.
  4. Do not go into rooms you do not need for the job.
  5. Do not open drawers, mail, papers or personal files.
  6. Do not bring anyone with you unless WilGlobo approved it in writing.
  7. Do not stay alone with a vulnerable person in a way that makes them uncomfortable. If you sense discomfort, step back and offer to involve a support person.
  8. Do not make jokes or comments about age, health, memory or ability.

4. Money and gifts

  1. Never take payment from a client. Clients pay WilGlobo directly.
  2. Never handle a client's cash, bank card, credit card or cheque.
  3. Never enter a client's card or bank details. The client types their own payment information.
  4. Do not accept cash tips. Do not accept gifts or favours beyond a coffee or a small snack offered during the visit. Politely say no to anything more and tell WilGlobo.
  5. Never borrow money from, lend money to, or sell anything to a client.
  6. Never be named in, witness, or help write a client's will, power of attorney or estate papers.
  7. Never give investment, banking, tax or financial advice.

5. Passwords and access

  1. Never ask for, write down, photograph or store a client's passwords or PINs.
  2. The client types their own passwords. If they need help remembering them, help them set up a password manager that they control.
  3. If a client tries to tell you a password, ask them to type it themselves instead.
  4. Never leave remote-access software installed unless the client has given written consent and WilGlobo approved it.
  5. Never create accounts in your own name for a client, or link a client's account to your email or phone.

6. No selling in the home

  1. Do not sell, quote or book any new paid work while you are in the home.
  2. Do not recommend a product because you or someone you know benefits from it.
  3. If the client wants more help, note it in the job status form. WilGlobo will follow up afterwards by phone, email or online.

This protects clients. Under the Alberta Consumer Protection Act, sales made in a person's home have special rules, including a cancellation right.

7. Scam spotting

Watch for these signs and tell the client gently:

  1. Pop-ups or calls saying their computer has a virus and asking them to call a number.
  2. Callers saying they are from a bank, CRA, police, Microsoft, Apple or a utility who ask for money or access.
  3. Requests to pay with gift cards, cryptocurrency or wire transfers.
  4. Emails or texts with urgent threats, prize wins or "grandchild in trouble" stories.
  5. Unknown remote-access apps on a device.

If you see any of these:

  1. Explain what you see in calm, plain words. Do not shame the client.
  2. Do not delete evidence without the client's permission.
  3. Suggest they call their bank using the number on their card.
  4. Point them to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre (1-888-495-8501).
  5. Note it in the job status form and tell Wilton the same day.

8. If you suspect abuse, neglect or an emergency

Medical emergency or danger

  1. Call 911 right away.
  2. Stay with the client if it is safe. Follow the dispatcher's instructions.
  3. Then call WilGlobo at 403-679-3039.
  4. Complete the Incident Report form the same day.

Possible financial abuse or neglect

Signs may include a stranger or relative controlling the client's money, new "friends" asking for access, unpaid bills, missing belongings, or a client who seems afraid, hungry or unwell and alone.

  1. Do not confront anyone.
  2. Do not investigate on your own.
  3. Write down what you saw and heard, with the date and time. Stick to facts.
  4. Tell Wilton the same day by phone, then use the Incident Report form.
  5. If the client is in immediate danger, call 911 first.

WilGlobo will decide on next steps. That may include contacting Alberta's Protection for Persons in Care line or other supports where the law allows.

9. Social media and public posts

  1. Never post photos, videos, names, addresses, screens or stories about a client or their home.
  2. This applies even if you hide faces or names, and even if the client says it is fine.
  3. Do not post about a job until WilGlobo has the client's written consent and approves the post.
  4. Do not speak for WilGlobo in public or to the media without written approval.

10. Professionalism

  1. Dress neatly and wear clean clothes suitable for the job.
  2. Use respectful language. No swearing.
  3. Keep personal phone use to a minimum during visits.
  4. Be honest about what you can and cannot do. If a task is beyond your skill or this code, stop and call WilGlobo.
  5. Report any mistake or damage right away. Honest mistakes are easier to fix when reported early.

11. Discrimination and harassment

  1. Treat every client, coworker and member of the public with respect.
  2. The Alberta Human Rights Act forbids discrimination based on race, religious beliefs, colour, gender, gender identity, gender expression, physical disability, mental disability, age, ancestry, place of origin, marital status, source of income, family status and sexual orientation.
  3. Do not harass anyone. This includes unwelcome comments, jokes, touching, or repeated contact.
  4. You also have the right to be treated with respect. If a client harasses or threatens you, leave safely and report it. See WK-SAFETY.

12. Conflicts of interest

  1. Tell WilGlobo if a client is a relative, friend or someone you already know.
  2. Tell WilGlobo if you have a business link to a product, store or service you might recommend.
  3. Do not use your work with us to win private work. See the non-solicitation clause in WK-AGREEMENT.

13. Confidentiality and AI

  1. Follow WK-PRIVACY for all client information.
  2. Follow AI-POLICY. Never put client personal information into a public AI tool.

14. Consequences

If you break this code, we may:

  1. talk with you and agree on a fix,
  2. stop offering you jobs for a period,
  3. end your agreement right away, as WK-AGREEMENT allows,
  4. report the matter to police or another authority where the law requires or allows.

Serious breaches, such as taking money, abusing a client or misusing passwords, lead to immediate termination.

Confidentiality and Privacy Undertaking

Version1.0
Effective dateOctober 6, 2026
Applies toAll contractors, service experts, temporary or seasonal workers and casual employees of WilGlobo Inc. (including TechCare by WilGlobo). Must be signed before first dispatch.

Prepared for: %%PREPARED_FOR%%

1. What this undertaking is

You will see personal information while you work for us. This includes names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, device contents, photos, account details and things clients say in their homes.

This undertaking is your promise to protect that information. It is part of your Worker Services Agreement (WK-AGREEMENT), or your Casual Employment Letter (WK-CASUAL) if you are a casual employee. It continues after your agreement ends.

2. The law in plain words

WilGlobo must follow Alberta's Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA). When information crosses provincial or national borders, the federal Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA) can also apply.

When you work for us, you act on our behalf. Our duties become your duties. In plain words:

  1. Only collect what the job needs.
  2. Only use it for the job.
  3. Only share it with WilGlobo, or with others WilGlobo approves.
  4. Keep it safe.
  5. Do not keep it longer than needed.

Our privacy contact is Wilton, Privacy Officer, tech@wilglobo.com, 403-679-3039.

3. What counts as confidential

  1. Any personal information about clients, their families, or other workers.
  2. Anything you see, hear or read in a client's home or on a client's device.
  3. WilGlobo business information that is not public, such as prices, client lists, processes, AI prompts and systems.

4. Minimum access

  1. Look only at what you need to do the task.
  2. Do not browse a client's photos, emails, messages, files or browser history.
  3. If you must open something to fix a problem, tell the client first and only look as long as needed.
  4. Do not ask clients personal questions that the job does not need.
  5. In WilGlobo systems (Airtable, Google), use only the access we give you. Your access is read-only. Never try to get more.

5. No copies

  1. Do not copy, photograph, screenshot, download, forward or print client information.
  2. If a screenshot is needed to fix a problem, ask the client first. Send it only to WilGlobo through the job status form. Then delete it from your device.
  3. Never take photos of the inside of a client's home unless WilGlobo asks for them for the job (for example, a TV mounting location) and the client agrees.

6. Your own devices

  1. Do not store client information on your personal phone, laptop, cloud drive or USB stick.
  2. Use the WilGlobo job status forms and calendar for job details. Do not keep separate notes or contact lists.
  3. Your phone and computer must have a screen lock, a passcode and current updates.
  4. Do not save client contact details in your personal contacts. If you must call a client, use the number in the job invite.
  5. Delete job texts and call logs that contain client details when the job is complete.

7. Passwords and payment details

  1. Never ask for, write down, photograph or store client passwords or PINs. The client types them.
  2. Never handle client card or bank details. The client enters their own payment information.
  3. See WK-CONDUCT for the full rules.

8. AI tools

  1. Never put client personal information into a public AI tool.
  2. Follow AI-POLICY for any AI use.

9. Information stored outside Canada

WilGlobo uses Airtable and Google. These are US-based service providers. Client and worker information may be stored or accessed in the United States and may be subject to US law. Do not move client information to any other service.

10. Reporting a privacy incident

A privacy incident is any time personal information is lost, stolen, seen by the wrong person, sent to the wrong person, or accessed without permission. Examples:

  1. You lose a phone that had a job text on it.
  2. You email a client's details to the wrong address.
  3. You see a client's private files by accident.
  4. A device you serviced is stolen from your vehicle.

What to do:

  1. Report it to Wilton the same day, and within 4 hours of finding out. Phone first: 403-679-3039. Then complete the Incident Report form.
  2. Do not try to fix it by yourself, except simple steps to stop more harm (for example, asking the wrong recipient to delete an email).
  3. Do not tell the client or anyone else before you talk to WilGlobo.
  4. Keep any evidence.

WilGlobo decides whether there is a real risk of significant harm. If there is, PIPA requires us to notify the Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Alberta without unreasonable delay. Your fast report makes that possible.

11. When you leave

When your agreement ends, or when we ask:

  1. Return any WilGlobo equipment, documents and ID badge.
  2. Delete any client information still on your devices, including texts, emails, photos and call logs.
  3. Confirm in writing that you have done so, within 5 business days.
  4. We will remove your access to WilGlobo systems.

Your duty to keep information confidential does not end.

12. If you break this undertaking

A breach may lead to immediate termination under WK-AGREEMENT. You may also be responsible for losses it causes, as WK-AGREEMENT sets out.

Health and Safety Rules

Version1.0
Effective dateOctober 6, 2026
Applies toAll contractors, service experts, temporary or seasonal workers and casual employees of WilGlobo Inc. (including TechCare by WilGlobo), especially anyone working in client homes. Must be signed before first dispatch.

Prepared for: %%PREPARED_FOR%%

1. Why these rules exist

Alberta's Occupational Health and Safety Act and OHS Code apply to work done in client homes. You are responsible for your own safety and the safety of others around you. WilGlobo is responsible for setting safe rules and a way to check on you when you work alone.

These rules are part of your Worker Services Agreement (WK-AGREEMENT), or your Casual Employment Letter (WK-CASUAL) if you are a casual employee.

2. Hazard check on arrival

Before you start work, take one minute to look around. Check:

  1. Is the entrance safe (ice, stairs, lighting, loose railings)?
  2. Are there pets? Are they calm and secured?
  3. Is anyone in the home acting aggressive, impaired or threatening?
  4. Is there a smell of gas, smoke or burning?
  5. Are cords, outlets or power bars damaged, hot or overloaded?
  6. Is the work area clear? Is there room to set up and to lift safely?
  7. Is there mould, pests, needles or other health hazards?
  8. Do you have the right tools and help for this job?

If anything is unsafe, fix it if it is simple and safe to do so. Otherwise stop, leave if needed, and call WilGlobo. Note the hazard in the job status form.

3. Your right to refuse

  1. You have the right to refuse work you believe is dangerous. This right is in the Alberta OHS Act.
  2. You will not be penalized for refusing in good faith.
  3. If you refuse, stop the work, make the area safe if you can, and tell WilGlobo right away.
  4. WilGlobo will look into it with you before anyone else is asked to do the task.

4. Working Alone check-in

Most of our home visits are done alone. OHS Code Part 28 requires a way to check on workers who work alone. Ours is:

  1. At arrival, mark "Arrived" in the job status form before you start.
  2. At departure, mark "Departed" in the job status form when you leave.
  3. If you will finish more than 30 minutes after the planned end time, choose "Running late" on the form and give your new finish time. This also tells WilGlobo you are safe.
  4. If you have not checked out, and have not sent a "Running late" update in the last 45 minutes, WilGlobo is alerted automatically 30 minutes after the planned end time. The check repeats every hour until you check out. When an alert comes in:
  5. WilGlobo calls your phone.
  6. If there is no answer within 10 more minutes, WilGlobo calls the client.
  7. If WilGlobo still cannot confirm you are safe, WilGlobo calls 911 and gives your last known location.
  8. Keep your phone charged and with you. Make sure WilGlobo has a current emergency contact for you.
  9. For visits that are higher risk (night visits, remote locations, known concerns), WilGlobo may set extra check-ins.

5. Ladders and heights

  1. Use a sturdy step stool or ladder that is the right height. Never stand on chairs, tables, counters or boxes.
  2. Inspect the ladder before use. Do not use it if any part is bent, cracked or loose.
  3. Set it on firm, level ground. Lock the spreaders fully.
  4. Keep three points of contact. Do not stand on the top two steps.
  5. Do not reach far to the side. Move the ladder instead.
  6. Do not use a ladder over 8 feet (2.4 m) on a TechCare job.

6. Lifting

  1. Do not lift more than you can handle safely. Never lift more than 23 kg (50 lb) alone. Get help for anything awkward.
  2. Bend your knees. Keep the load close. Do not twist while lifting.
  3. Never ask a client to help lift.
  4. Plan your path before you lift. Clear tripping hazards.

7. TV mounting rules

  1. Mount only on wood studs or solid masonry using hardware rated for the TV's weight. Never mount to drywall alone.
  2. Use a stud finder. Confirm the stud by a small pilot hole in the planned spot.
  3. Never drill blind near outlets, switches, light fixtures, plumbing or gas lines. Stay at least 15 cm (6 in) away from them. Use a stud finder with live-wire detection.
  4. Check the mount, bolts and bracket are rated for the TV's weight and size.
  5. A second person must help lift and hang any TV 55 inches or larger, or over 23 kg (50 lb). Do not do it alone.
  6. Do not mount above a fireplace, on a brick chimney, or on any surface you are not sure of. Call WilGlobo instead.
  7. Do not run power cables inside walls unless using a code-approved in-wall power kit, and only if WilGlobo has approved it for that job.
  8. Test the mount by pulling gently before you let go of the TV.

8. Work you must never do

  1. No electrical work. Do not open panels, replace outlets or switches, or wire anything into the home's power. This needs a licensed electrician under Alberta's Safety Codes Act.
  2. No gas work of any kind.
  3. No structural work. Do not cut studs, joists or load-bearing walls.
  4. No roof work.
  5. If a job needs any of these, stop. Tell WilGlobo. We will advise the client to hire a licensed trade.

9. Driving

  1. Driving to and from jobs is your responsibility. Hold a valid licence and insurance for business use.
  2. Obey all traffic laws. Do not use a handheld phone while driving.
  3. Do not drive impaired or overtired.
  4. In winter, carry an emergency kit and allow extra time.
  5. Do not leave client devices visible in your vehicle.

10. Infection control

  1. Do not attend a visit if you have a fever, cough, vomiting or other signs of a contagious illness. Tell WilGlobo as early as you can.
  2. Wash or sanitize your hands on arrival and before you leave.
  3. Wear a mask if the client asks.
  4. Wipe down shared devices, keyboards and remotes before and after use when practical.

11. Aggressive animals or people

  1. If an animal or a person makes you feel unsafe, leave right away. You do not need permission.
  2. Do not argue or try to calm a dangerous situation on your own.
  3. Once safe, call 911 if anyone is in danger. Then call WilGlobo.
  4. Mark "Departed" in the job status form and note why.

12. First aid

  1. Carry a basic personal first aid kit in your vehicle.
  2. Know the address of the job in case you need to call 911.
  3. For any serious injury to you or anyone else, call 911 first.
  4. A current first aid certificate is recommended, but not required.

13. Reporting incidents

Report all of these using the Incident Report form the same day:

  1. Any injury to you, a client or anyone else, even a small one.
  2. Any near miss (something that almost caused harm).
  3. Any damage to client property.
  4. Any threat, harassment or unsafe situation.

Call WilGlobo at 403-679-3039 first for anything serious. Serious injuries and some incidents must be reported to Alberta OHS. WilGlobo will handle that report. If you have your own WCB coverage, you must also report to WCB-Alberta as required.

Privacy Policy

Version1.0
Effective dateOctober 6, 2026
Applies toAll services of WilGlobo Inc. (including TechCare by WilGlobo), our websites, clients, prospective clients, newsletter subscribers and workers

1. Who we are

This policy explains how WilGlobo Inc. (including TechCare by WilGlobo) handles personal information. In this policy, "we" means WilGlobo Inc. and "you" means the person whose information we hold.

We offer:

  1. TechCare by WilGlobo (techcares.ca): hands-on tech help in your home in Calgary.
  2. Digital and AI consulting for small businesses and nonprofits.
  3. Creative and media services.

Our address is 105 26 Ave SW, Calgary, Alberta, Canada. Our websites are techcares.ca (TechCare) and wilglobo.com (WilGlobo).

2. The laws we follow

We follow Alberta's Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA). When personal information moves across provincial or national borders as part of our business, the federal Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA) may also apply. We send commercial emails and texts in line with Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation (CASL).

3. Our privacy contact

We have named a person to answer privacy questions and requests.

  • Name: Wilton, Privacy Officer
  • Email: tech@wilglobo.com
  • Phone: 403-679-3039
  • Mail: WilGlobo Inc., Attention: Privacy Officer, 105 26 Ave SW, Calgary, AB

4. What we collect

We collect only what we need to do the work you ask for.

Clients and prospective clients

  • Name, address, phone number and email.
  • The name and contact details of a family member or helper, if you give them to us.
  • Details of the job: what devices you have, what went wrong, what we did, and notes from the visit.
  • Booking, invoice and payment records. Our payment processors handle your card details. We do not see or keep your full card number.
  • Signed forms and the date, time and version of each form you signed.
  • Your choices about receiving news and offers from us.

Business clients

  • Contact names, roles and work contact details.
  • Information you share with us so we can deliver a project.

Workers

  • Name, contact details and emergency contact.
  • Business details needed to pay you, such as a GST number and payment details.
  • Job assignments, status updates, signed agreements and training records.
  • Workers' Compensation Board (WCB) clearance letters and safety records.

What we do not collect

  • We never ask for, write down or keep your passwords or PINs. You type them yourself.
  • We never take your bank or card details to make a purchase for you. You enter your own payment information.
  • We do not collect government ID numbers unless a law requires it.

5. Why we collect it

We use personal information to:

  1. Book, deliver and follow up on the services you ask for.
  2. Send job confirmations, reminders and invoices.
  3. Take payment and keep business and tax records.
  4. Keep you, our workers and your home safe.
  5. Assign jobs to workers and pay them.
  6. Answer questions and handle complaints.
  7. Send news and offers, but only if you agreed to receive them.
  8. Meet our legal duties.

We do not sell personal information. We do not rent or trade mailing lists.

6. How we get your consent

We ask for your consent when we collect your information, unless the law allows otherwise.

  • Express consent: you tell us yes, for example by signing a form or ticking a box.
  • Implied consent: the purpose is obvious and you give us the information, for example your address so we can come to your home.

You can withdraw consent at any time by contacting our privacy contact. We will tell you if this means we cannot provide a service. You can stop marketing messages at any time with the unsubscribe link or by replying STOP to a text.

If someone helps you manage your affairs, such as a family member with power of attorney, they may give consent for you. We may ask to see proof of their authority.

7. Who we share it with

We share personal information only when needed:

  1. With the worker assigned to your job. They see only what they need to do it.
  2. With service providers who store data or run tools for us (see section 8).
  3. With a family member or helper you have named.
  4. When the law requires it, or in an emergency where someone's health or safety is at risk.

8. Service providers outside Canada

We use outside companies to run our business. Some store or process personal information outside Canada. When information is outside Canada, the laws of that country apply, and courts or government agencies there may be able to access it.

You can ask us about our use of service providers outside Canada. Contact our privacy contact (section 3). We will explain how we handle and protect the information.

9. How we protect it

We use reasonable safeguards:

  • Accounts protected with strong passwords and two-step sign-in.
  • Access limited to the people who need it for their work.
  • Workers sign confidentiality rules before their first job.
  • No client personal information goes into public or consumer AI tools.
  • Paper notes are not kept. If any are made, they are shredded.
  • Lost or stolen devices are reported at once.

No system is perfect. If a breach creates a real risk of significant harm to you, we will report it to the Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Alberta and tell you as required.

10. How long we keep it

We keep personal information only as long as we reasonably need it for business or legal reasons. For example:

  • Financial records: 6 years, as the Canada Revenue Agency requires.
  • Signed forms: for as long as we work with you, plus 6 years.
  • Marketing consent records: while consent is active, plus a set period after you unsubscribe.

When we no longer need it, we delete it securely or make it anonymous.

11. Seeing and correcting your information

You can ask to see the personal information we hold about you. You can also ask us to correct it.

  1. Send your request in writing to our privacy contact.
  2. We may ask you to confirm who you are.
  3. We will answer within 45 days. If we need more time, we will tell you why, as the law allows.
  4. If we cannot give you some of the information, we will tell you why.

There is no charge for a request to see your own information.

12. Questions and complaints

Please contact our privacy contact first. We will try to fix the problem.

If you are not satisfied, you have the right to contact the Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Alberta (OIPC). Time limits can apply, so contact them soon after our response.

  • Website: oipc.ab.ca
  • Phone: 780-422-6860 or toll free 1-888-878-4044

Where PIPEDA applies, you can also contact the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada at priv.gc.ca.

13. How we use AI

We use AI tools to help draft messages, plan schedules, sort requests and create content. A person always checks the work and makes the decision. We never put client personal information, passwords or photos into public or consumer AI tools. We do not use AI to make decisions about you. Read our AI Use Policy (AI-POLICY) for details.

14. Our websites

Our websites are techcares.ca and wilglobo.com. They may use basic, privacy-friendly analytics to count visits. These tools may collect your device type, browser and general location. They do not tell us your name.

We do not use advertising cookies and we do not sell data.

You can block or delete cookies in your browser settings.

15. Changes to this policy

We may update this policy. The new version will show a new effective date. If a change affects how we use information you already gave us, we will tell you and ask for consent where needed.

Service Terms, Pricing and Complaints

Version1.0
Effective dateOctober 6, 2026
Applies toAll TechCare clients and the public. For reference. No signature needed.

1. About us

WilGlobo Inc., operating as TechCare by WilGlobo ("TechCare" or "we"), helps adults in Calgary with home technology. We come to your home. We explain things in plain words and go at your pace.

  • Address: 105 26 Ave SW, Calgary, Alberta
  • Email: tech@wilglobo.com
  • Phone: 403-679-3039
  • Website: techcares.ca

2. Our prices

We charge per task. We always tell you the price and confirm it with you before work starts.

Basic tasks: $35 to $45

  • Installing apps
  • Setting up email
  • Help with buying a device or service
  • Following up with your subscription or service companies
  • Help with buying or renting a device

Advanced tasks: from $55

  • Windows installation
  • Troubleshooting
  • Wi-Fi and network setup
  • TV setup
  • TV mounting

Other ways to pay for help

  • Per project: we quote the price in writing before any work starts.
  • Packages: we quote what the package includes and its price in writing before any work starts.
  • Hourly: we quote the hourly rate in writing before any work starts.

3. Why a price can change

Some jobs turn out to be bigger than expected. A price may be higher if:

  • The device is old, slow or has many problems
  • More than one device or account is involved
  • The task needs extra parts, cables or a mount
  • The wall or space makes mounting harder
  • A service company keeps us on hold for a long time

If this happens, we stop and tell you first. You decide whether to go ahead. We never add a charge without your agreement.

4. How to pay

  • You pay WilGlobo Inc. directly, never the worker.
  • We accept debit or credit card (processed by Square or Stripe) or Interac e-Transfer. Details are on your invoice.
  • Payment is due when the task is completed, unless we agree otherwise in writing before the work starts.
  • You will get a receipt.

5. GST

If GST applies to your service, it is shown separately on your quote and invoice.

6. No selling in your home

Our workers will not sell you new paid work or book new paid jobs during a visit. If you need more help, we will send you a quote by phone, email or online afterwards. You can decide in your own time.

7. Cancelling and missed visits

  • Please give us at least 24 hours' notice if you need to cancel or move your visit.
  • There is no fee for cancelling or for a missed visit.
  • If late cancellations or missed visits happen more than twice, we may ask for payment before future visits.
  • If we need to cancel, we will call you as soon as we can and rebook at no cost to you.

8. If the fix does not hold

If the same problem we fixed comes back within 14 days, we will come back and fix it at no charge. This does not cover new problems, changes made by someone else, damage, or other companies' products or services.

Products and subscriptions from other companies are covered by their own warranties, not ours.

9. If you are not happy

We want to hear from you. Here is what to do.

  1. Contact us. Call 403-679-3039 or email tech@wilglobo.com. A family member or support person can contact us for you.
  2. We reply. We will get back to you within 2 business days.
  3. We look into it. We will talk to you and the worker, and suggest a fix within 10 business days.
  4. Ask for the owner. If you are still not happy, ask for Wilton, the owner. He will review it and reply within 10 business days.

If you have a privacy concern, you can also contact the Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Alberta. For other consumer concerns, you can contact Alberta's consumer protection office (Service Alberta). Your rights under the Alberta Consumer Protection Act always apply.

10. Accessibility

  • You can ask for any of our documents in large print.
  • We are happy to read documents out loud with you.
  • You are welcome to have a family member, friend or support person with you at any visit.
  • Tell us if you need more time, a quieter visit, or anything else to make things easier.

11. Our safety promises

  • We never ask for, write down or keep your passwords or PINs.
  • We never handle your bank or card details.
  • We never accept gifts, loans or cash for ourselves.
  • We never give financial, legal or investment advice.
  • We never call you out of the blue asking for passwords, payment or remote access.
